answer: In an agent marketplace trading goods such as umber pigment, quill pens and dune maps, each seller identity must lock 100 tokens in a smart contract for 30 days before accepting orders. Creating 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month. The bond does not prove identities are unique, but it makes each additional active identity consume scarce capital, so spawning accounts cannot expand an attack for free.
